title: Price integer transvections on the shear target B^k.
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Scoped moment calculation for one larger shear alphabet. No new κ, no supplier admission, and no selected-frontier change. The selected conditional exponent remains `0.001672660197076918`.

PR #4126 shows that the unit alphabet `{X, X^{-1}, Y, Y^{-1}}` makes every faithful word for `B^k` fail the strict supplier test. This package prices the explicitly larger alphabet of arbitrary integer transvections

```text
X^t = [[1, t], [0, 1]],    Y^t = [[1, 0], [t, 1]],    t in Z, t != 0,
```

each letter one rank-1 child, with the same address width `m = 2` and the same moment `M(a) = (λ/W)·2^{a-1}`. The three-bit quotient is not used as a bill.

For `B = X^2 Y^2` and every integer `k ≥ 1`:

- `λ(B) = 2` via `X^2 Y^2`.
- `λ(B^k) ≥ 4` for every `k ≥ 2`, because a length-2 word needs a diagonal entry equal to 1 and a length-3 word needs `v_k` to divide `u_{k-1}-1`, while `0 < u_{k-1}-1 < v_k`. The word `(X^2 Y^2)^k` gives `λ(B^k) ≤ 2k`.
- At `W = 2`, the single matrix `B` satisfies `M(a) = 2^{a-1} < 1` for every `a ∈ [0, 1)`, and `M(1) = 1`. Every higher power fails the strict test.
- At `W = 1` the strict test already fails for `B`.
- Re-expanding each coefficient into `|t|` unit shears restores length 4 for `B` and removes the `W = 2` pass.

Status: partial. The length classification is a proof for every `k`; the verifier checks the identities it uses through `B^{24}`. This is not a register identity, not a native XOR bill, and not a multiplication theorem.

## Task and overlap

Base commit `bb4bccbf42844d2801487450727c2f63e10d1d0f`. Catalogue card `bit-new-register-model`, priority revision 6. Scope key `7084092dd726e7ba1f2f` for the card method “Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.”

**Scope: changed.** The card asks for a new register identity escaping the three-register obstruction. This package does not build that identity. It answers open question 1 of the unit-shear supplier inequality, a different object on the same bit-mechanism track. An optimistic pass for one matrix at one role count is not catalogue acceptance.

Nearest work:

- #3905 introduces `B` and the four-call unit word.
- #3937 and #3947 give the commutative obstruction and the three-bit quotient. The quotient’s conversion cost stays unpriced and is not reused.
- #4126 proves `λ ≥ 2k+1` for unit letters and asks for a larger integer alphabet. This PR is that alphabet. It does not repeat the unit-letter proof.
- #4118 and #4119 are other `bit-new-register-model` packages (span-four dirty auxiliary, span-six flagged exclusion). They do not price this shear alphabet.

Session selection: eligible open handoffs on Discussion #1166, after excluding work already delivered this round, numbered from 1 so sibling sessions keep items 1–10. Fewer than 27 eligible items remained. Item index `(27-1) mod 12 = 2` is the shear supplier/recurrence inequality (comments 19031016 and 19032401). #4126 already performed that item, so this PR is the distinct larger-alphabet remainder.

## Validation

Environment: Python 3.12.3, standard library only. No Lean, Docker, or selected cold replay.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/sl2z-transvection-moment
```

Also run under `python3.12 -I -O -Werror -B`. Observed:

```text
PASS_SL2Z_TRANSVECTION_MOMENT powers=24 lambda(B)=2 lambda(B^k)>=4_for_k>=2 W2_passes_on_[0,1) W1_fails powers_fail no_new_kappa
PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/sl2z-transvection-moment outcome=partial
```

The finite script checks the recurrence, the word `(X^2 Y^2)^k`, the determinant and companion identities, both closed forms on a sample of exponents, the unit breadth-first control (length 4), the strict moment on every rational in `[0, 1]` with denominator at most 8, rejection of the boundary `M = 1`, and a damaged coefficient. The claim for every `k` is the divisibility argument in `research/sl2z-transvection-moment/README.md`. Exact `λ(B^k) = 2k` is not claimed.

## Credit

- **ToikY with OpenAI Codex**, PRs #3937 and #3947: commutative obstruction, three-bit quotient, and the request for a supplier inequality.
- **unpaidmoon**, PR #4126: unit-alphabet inequality and the open question this package answers.

Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance. Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

Package question 1: if a coefficient `t = 2` is one shift plus a unit shear, rather than one child or two unit children, does `M(a) < 1` still hold for `B` at `W = 2`? That price decides which of the two extremes this alphabet lands on. First step: name one native operation that implements the shift, charge its rank and any dirty auxiliary, and recompute the two-role moment. Blocker: the rank-only model has no such native shift. Inventing one would be a new alphabet.

## Workflow feedback (optional)

Handoff-first selection on Discussion #1166, then a one-alphabet stop after both role readings, matched the package guide. Feedback thread: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1200
